title: Plan and execute processes for the representative sampling of a seed lot

lessons.title: Planning a seed lot sampling
lessons.html:
Before you go to the warehouse

Seed sampling is usually done at a seed company's processing plant or warehouse, often for certification or before sale. A planned visit avoids wasted time and invalid samples.

Gather information

  • Species and cultivar, lot numbers, lot sizes and container types (bags, mini-bulk bags, bulk).
  • Purpose of sampling: certification, ISTA certificate, internal quality control or export.
  • Tests requested, which affect sample size and packaging (for example, moisture requires moisture-proof containers).
  • Whether the seed is treated, and with what.

Check the rules

Use the current ISTA rules and national scheme requirements to confirm:

  • The maximum lot size for the species; a larger lot must be split.
  • The sampling intensity: how many primary samples are required for the number of containers or the mass in bulk.
  • The minimum submitted sample mass for the tests required.

Prepare equipment

  • Correct triers for the seed size: stick triers for bags or bulk, Nobbe triers for bags, hand sampling for chaffy seed.
  • Clean containers for the composite sample.
  • Divider, if reducing on site.
  • Sample bags or containers, seals, labels and sampling forms.
  • Gloves, dust mask and eye protection for treated seed.

Arrange access

Ask the company to arrange the lot so that containers can be reached from different positions, with lot labels visible. If containers are stacked so that only the outside can be reached, the sample may not be representative; insist on access or document the limitation as the rules require.

Safety in warehouses

Watch for forklifts, unstable stacks and dust. Never climb on stacks without a safe platform. Wear your protective equipment when handling treated seed and wash hands before eating.

lessons.title: Executing the sampling
lessons.html:
On site

1. Verify the lot

  • Check that all containers carry the same lot number and correct labelling.
  • Count containers and confirm the lot size.
  • Look for signs of non-uniformity: different bag types, colours, treatment colours, damaged containers.

If the lot appears non-uniform, do not sample it as one lot; report to the client and record the observation. The rules provide a heterogeneity test where doubt exists.

2. Take primary samples

  1. Select containers spread through the lot, not just the accessible ones.
  2. Take primary samples from top, middle and bottom positions as appropriate.
  3. Insert the trier closed, open it to fill, close and withdraw, then empty into the composite container.
  4. Check that primary samples look similar; marked differences suggest non-uniformity.

3. Form and reduce the composite sample

Mix the primary samples into the composite sample. If it is larger than needed, reduce it to the submitted sample size with a riffle, conical or centrifugal divider, or by an approved method for the species. Never reduce by scooping off a portion.

4. Pack, seal and label

  • Use moisture-proof containers when moisture is to be determined, filled to minimise air space.
  • Seal so tampering is evident.
  • Label with species, cultivar, lot number, sample number, date and your name.

5. Document

Complete the sampling report: lot details, number of containers, number of primary samples, method, instruments, observations and seal numbers. Get the client representative to sign if required.

6. Dispatch

Send samples promptly to the laboratory. Protect them from heat, damp and direct sun in the vehicle.

Typical errors to avoid

ErrorEffect
Sampling only outside bagsUnrepresentative sample
Wrong trier for seed sizeSeed damage or biased sampling
Non-moisture-proof packagingInvalid moisture result
Unlabelled sampleResult cannot be traced; sample rejected

Key points

  • Plan species, lot size, tests and equipment from the current rules.
  • Verify lot identity and uniformity before sampling.
  • Sample containers spread through the lot at different positions.
  • Reduce only with approved dividers or methods.
  • Seal, label, document and dispatch samples promptly.
